name: Bewildering Koan — Additional Material (d20pfsrd)
body:
More on Bewildering Koan from d20pfsrd.com.

These sections appear on d20pfsrd.com's page "Bewildering Koan" but are not part of the Bewildering Koan entry, which is unchanged.

Editor’s Note

The type of check is not specified, but typically Bluff checks are opposed by Sense Motive, so we feel it’s likely what is required here.

GMs may wish to reword the text of the second sentence as:

“The target may attempt an opposed Sense Motive check, and if the creature fails its check…”

Sean K Reynolds wrote: Bluff is always an opposed check against the target’s Sense Motive check. If the target fails, it loses its next turn.
